originalTitle: US stocks: US market opens mixed as investors weigh Middle East tensions, data
simplifiedContent: The US stock market started the day with mixed results on Friday. This means that some stocks went up and some went down. The market was still reacting to the fact that the S&P 500, a key measure of the market, had reached a record high the day before. Investors were also thinking about some new economic data, like retail sales, and what's happening in the Middle East. The main stock indexes, like the Dow Jones and the S&P 500, actually started the day a bit higher, but the overall mood was uncertain.

originalTitle: Cochin Shipyard Q1 Results: Profit falls 19% YoY to Rs 151 crore, revenue up marginally
simplifiedContent: Cochin Shipyard, a company that builds ships, recently released its financial report for the first quarter of the year. Unfortunately, the company's profit decreased by 19% compared to the same time last year, which means it made less money. However, the company's revenue, or the total amount of money it brought in, increased slightly. The company's profit margins were also affected, and it had to pay some fines due to issues with its board of directors. This news matters because it shows how the company is performing and can help investors decide whether to buy or sell its stocks.

originalTitle: Sebi revises InvIT cash flow framework to allow adding back external debt-funded maintenance costs
simplifiedContent: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has made a change to the rules for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), which are companies that invest in infrastructure projects like roads. Now, InvITs that own road projects can add back the costs of borrowing money to pay for maintenance, which will help them manage these costs better. This means InvITs will have more flexibility to take care of their projects. However, if an InvIT wants to take on new debt for maintenance, it will need to get approval from its unitholders and be transparent about the debt and maintenance expenses. This change is important because it allows InvITs to handle maintenance costs in a more efficient way.

originalTitle: US stocks mixed after retail sales data, Middle East in focus
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the main groups of US stocks, called the Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq, had a mixed day. The Dow Jones barely went up, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq went up a bit more. This happened after some new information came out about how much people are spending money in stores. The stock market is also keeping an eye on what's happening in the Middle East. These small changes in the stock market are a sign that investors are waiting to see what happens next before making big decisions.

originalTitle: Dollar deluge prompts RBI to shut special FCNR scheme early; $52 bn raised so far
simplifiedContent: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to stop a special program that allowed people to invest foreign money in India. This program, called the FCNR scheme, was supposed to keep going, but the RBI is shutting it down early because a lot of money has already come in. So far, $52 billion has been raised through this program. The RBI's governor had said just last week that they didn't plan to close the program early, but it seems they've changed their mind. This matters because it shows that the RBI is taking steps to manage the large amount of foreign money flowing into India.

originalTitle: Pulse of the Street: Tata jitters, metal rout weigh on Indian equities
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market went down by 0.8% this week. This happened because investors were worried about who will lead the Tata company next, and also because the prices of metals like steel and copper were falling. Even though some companies like telecom and real estate did well, it wasn't enough to make the whole market go up. This meant that India's stock market didn't do as well as other countries in Asia, where stocks were rising because of advancements in artificial intelligence. Overall, it was a bit of a tough week for the Indian stock market.
